messages:
From: Lara Green <lara.green@keepsake.health>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal request and concessions — Keepsake Health (KSK)

Hi Ava,

We're approaching renewal for Keepsake Health (Deal KSK-2029-059) and I wanted to get a formal request on file before our finance window closes May 10. Our board is asking for a more favorable renewal given last quarter's incident and shifting budget timing. Specific asks are below: 

- 40% one-time term discount on the next 12-month renewal invoice
- $60,000 one-time credit to offset incident impact and migration costs
- 6-month term reset (push renewal date from July to January)
- SLA add-on (99.95% uptime warranty with a 6-month penalty/credit clause)

We appreciate the reliability improvements your team shipped, and we want to continue with Redwood, but these concessions are critical for the renewal to go through. I attached a short note from our CFO and usage highlights.

Can you let me know if Redwood can accommodate any of these items, and who on your side needs to sign off? We're happy to join a quick call this week.

Thanks,
Lara Green
Head of Procurement, Keepsake Health
Attachments: Keepsake_Renewal_Request.pdf (pdf)

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Green <lara.green@keepsake.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Apr 2029 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal request and concessions — Keepsake Health (KSK)

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear note and for attaching the CFO statement.

We value Keepsake as a partner and I want to be transparent: the asks you listed are outside our standard renewal authority. I’d like to align internally on what we can offer quickly so we can get a proposal over to you.

I’ve looped in Karthik (AM) and Marissa (VP Sales) to assess concession authority and next steps. Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow at 10am PT to walk through usage and the specific impact you’re citing? If that timing doesn’t work, suggest two alternatives.

Best,
Ava Chen

ava.chen@redwood.ai

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Apr 2029 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Keepsake Health renewal — request for non-standard concessions (needs exec/desk approval)

Team — following Lara's request (attached), Keepsake is asking for a sizable package to re-up. Summary of asks: 40% discount, $60k credit, 6-month term reset, SLA 99.95% add-on.

Why this matters: Keepsake is mid-market, steady growth, but we saw churn risk after the outage in Q1. They are an advocate in their space and have expansion potential (embedding usage is increasing ~18% q/q). If we lose them, the revenue gap and momentum loss in the health vertical is non-trivial.

Proposed concession options for decision: 
- Option A (conservative): 25% one-time discount, $25k credit, 3-month term reset, 6-month SLA add-on
- Option B (compromise): 35% one-time discount, $50k credit, 6-month term reset, 12-month SLA add-on
- Option C (aggressive, needs exec signoff): 40% discount, $60k credit, 6-month term reset, 12-month SLA add-on + penalty clause

My recommended starting ask to Keepsake is Option B — more likely to close while protecting margin. I need authority to offer Option B or confirmation of whatever you approve. Please respond with "Approve Option X" / "Modify" / "Decline".

I've attached a usage extract to help with the economics. If we approve Option B, legal will need to draft an amendment and finance must prepare a one-time credit.

Attachments: Keepsake_usage_report.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Ava

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2029 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Keepsake Health renewal — request for non-standard concessions (needs exec/desk approval)

Thanks for the summary, Ava. I reviewed the usage and the incident timeline. Keepsake is strategic for our health vertical, but we must keep a guardrail on discount depth and absolute dollars committed.

I am willing to approve a modified package without needing CEO-level signoff:
- 25% one-time discount
- $25,000 one-time credit
- 6-month SLA add-on (no penalty clause)
- 3-month term reset

Rationale: protects YoY revenue while demonstrating good will. Anything beyond this (more credit or >30% discount or 12-month SLA penalty language) requires VP Sales or CRO approval.

If you need me to field this to the customer, I can present this as a near-term offer and say we can escalate for additional consideration. Marking as APPROVE (with limits).

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Sales Operations
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2029 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Keepsake Health renewal — request for non-standard concessions (needs exec/desk approval)

Team / Keepsake — after reviewing the economics and risk, I am authorizing a one-time settlement package to preserve the relationship and buy us time for expansion discussions. Approved concessions (final):

- 30% one-time discount on the upcoming 12-month renewal invoice
- $40,000 one-time credit applied at renewal
- 6-month term reset (next renewal window will be Jan 31, 2030)
- SLA add-on: 99.95% uptime warranty for 12 months (no punitive SLA penalties; credits only)

Action items:
- Legal: prepare contract amendment reflecting the above and include a one-time credit line (file: Keepsake_contract_amendment_draft.docx). Please target a first draft by EOD Wednesday.
- Finance: prepare the credit memo and ensure invoicing aligns to the new renewal date.
- Ava/Karthik: present this package to Keepsake and secure acknowledgement; if Keepsake asks for anything beyond what’s approved above, escalate to me with clear ask and customer rationale.

This approval is made under VP Sales authority — I expect us to protect margin where possible and tie the concession to a 12-month expansion QBR with Keepsake (add a customer success checkpoint).

Marissa Cole
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
